title: Conduit chat shim: compatibility mapper for legacy chat API and structured tool calls
creator: Anika Rao
description: Create a resilient, testable compatibility shim (Conduit) that maps legacy OpenAI-style Chat Completions requests/responses to Redwood's internal streaming and tool/function-calling model format. The shim should accept incoming requests from customers using older Chat Completions semantics (role/message arrays, top_p, presence_penalty, functions array, stop tokens, etc.), translate them into Redwood internal RPCs, and map streaming deltas and final structured outputs back into the legacy response shapes. Aim to make the adapter lossless for common tool-calling and structured-output use cases while preserving Redwood streaming behavior and observability hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Shim accepts POST /v1/chat/completions OpenAI-style payload and returns a 200 with legacy-shaped response when model supports parity
Streaming path: server-sent events (SSE) & chunked responses produce delta tokens and function_call events matching legacy ordering expectations

Tool/function calls: functions[] in request are invoked via Redwood toolhook interface and the returned function call payload is surfaced in the response in the legacy 'finish_reason: function_call' style
Structured outputs: JSON schema enforcement and structured output metadata are preserved and surfaced in both streaming deltas and final message content
Edge cases: partial failures (tool timeouts, model fallback, truncated kv cache) return clear legacy-compliant error frames and non-ambiguous finish_reason
Automated integration tests cover request mappings, streaming deltas, tool call roundtrips, and failure modes
No customer-visible latency regression >10ms p50 on the hosted path compared to native requests (measured on internal perf harness)
technical_notes: Map input role/message arrays -> internal prompt builder; preserve metadata (user/system/assistant) and message ids for traceability
Translate top_p/temperature/nucleus sampling to runtime-compatible sampling knobs; document any quantization of tuning granularity

Streaming: Redwood emits token deltas and structured events. For legacy SSE, synthesize 'data: {"choices": [{"delta":{...}}] }' frames while maintaining event ordering. Use incremental content-length framing for HTTP chunked fallback

Function/tool calls: when model returns function_call in streaming deltas, buffer until the tool payload is complete or function_call.end event arrives; then emit legacy-style function_call object in final choice and include tool output as a subsequent assistant message when applicable

Finish reasons: map internal finish reasons to legacy enumerations (stop, length, function_call, content_filter, error); include both 'finish_reason' and an 'x-redwood-reason' header for observability

Backpressure & batching: respect request-level max_tokens and runtime batching policies; ensure that we do not expose internal batching to the client but surface token-level streaming in the same cadence as native legacy providers
Error mapping: translate infra/model errors into OpenAI-compatible error codes and messages. Rate limit responses must match legacy 429 body format when applicable
Auth & headers: accept legacy API keys on the shim endpoint and map them to internal tenant ID; propagate tracing headers (x-rw-trace) into runtime requests
Observability: attach token-level metrics and event markers for canary toggles; log full request/response mapping decisions to debug-only traces behind feature flag
api_examples: Shim → internal RPC (conceptual): Conduit buffers messages → builds prompt bundle with message ids → attaches functions metadata → calls runtime/streaming endpoint with trace headers

Example outgoing delta SSE frame: data: {"id":"chatcmpl-abc", "object":"chat.completion.chunk", "created":1670, "choices":[{"delta":{"content":"The article covers", "function_call":null}, "index":0, "finish_reason":null}]}
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged deploy to staging Conduit endpoint; run full integration harness against dev customers' sample prompts
Internal canary: expose shim to 5 production accounts behind opt-in; collect latency, token correctness, and tool-call fidelity metrics for 72h
Expand to 25% of incoming legacy-key traffic if no regressions; monitor error rates and structured-output mismatches
Full rollout after 2 weeks and sign-off from reliability, DX, and security teams
Post-rollout: add backward-compat validation to Console that shows when a customer uses legacy semantics and flags potential behavioral deltas
tests: Unit tests for input mapping: role preservation, message id propagation, sampling parameter translation
Integration tests: streaming delta ordering, partial-function-call buffering, function_call roundtrip with mocked toolhook
Contract tests: ensure legacy response shape matches schema in agents.md examples and Confluence contract doc
Performance tests: p50/p95 latency against perf harness with native and shimmed requests, target <10ms difference
Chaos tests: simulated toolhook timeouts, model fallback, and kv cache eviction to verify clear legacy error frames
